# Implementation Plan: Innovation Portal

**Branch**: `1-innovation-portal` | **Date**: 2026-02-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)  
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/1-innovation-portal/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command.

## Summary

Build a full-stack Innovation Portal web application using Next.js where authenticated users can submit innovation ideas with file attachments, track status through a four-state lifecycle (Submitted → Under Review → Accepted → Rejected), and administrators can evaluate ideas with audit-trailed feedback. The system uses PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM for persistence, NextAuth.js for session management, and Multer for file uploads, with RBAC distinguishing regular users from admins.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x with Node.js 20 LTS (Next.js mandated by constitution)  
**Primary Dependencies**: Next.js 14 (App Router), NextAuth.js 5, Prisma 5, Multer 1.x, bcrypt 5, PostgreSQL 16, Zod (input validation), Tailwind CSS  
**Storage**: PostgreSQL (relational data + attachment metadata), local filesystem via Multer for uploaded files (`/uploads/` directory)  
**Testing**: Jest + React Testing Library (unit/integration), Playwright (E2E), minimum 80% coverage enforced  
**Target Platform**: Node.js 20 web server (Docker-deployable), browser clients  
**Project Type**: Web application (full-stack — Next.js App Router handles both frontend pages and API routes)  
**Performance Goals**: Dashboard page < 2 s for ≤ 100 ideas; file upload < 10 MB; 50 concurrent users without degradation  
**Constraints**: bcrypt minimum 10 rounds; pagination 20 ideas/page; file-type verified via MIME detection server-side; audit trail never deleted for status changes  
**Scale/Scope**: ~50 concurrent users, hundreds of ideas initially; paginated dashboard (20/page)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| I. Documentation-First | ✅ PASS | Spec fully written and approved before any implementation |
| II. Quality Standards | ✅ PASS | TypeScript strict mode, ESLint, 80% coverage gate, peer reviews required |
| III. Service Boundaries | ⚠️ JUSTIFIED | Constitution mandates "Microservices" architecture; this feature is ONE portal microservice (Next.js app). Future services (e.g., notification, analytics) will communicate via API. Internal API routes (`/api/**`) are the explicit contract boundary; no direct DB access across services |
| IV. Security-First | ✅ PASS | NextAuth.js for auth, bcrypt ≥10 rounds, Zod input validation, MIME detection, SQL-injection-safe via Prisma parameterised queries, XSS prevention via React DOM escaping |
| V. Test Coverage | ✅ PASS | Unit (business logic), integration (DB + API routes), E2E (Playwright for critical user flows). 80% coverage enforced in CI |

**Gate result**: PASS (with documented justification for microservices scope)

**Structure Decision**: Single Next.js service (App Router) acting as the innovation portal microservice. API routes under `/api/` form the explicit service boundary. This is constitutional because the portal is one microservice; future services connect via these API contracts.

## Complexity Tracking

> Violations with justification

| Violation | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|-----------|------------|--------------------------------------|
| Microservices declared in constitution but single Next.js app used | One portal is the entire scope of this feature; splitting into separate frontend + backend services adds operational complexity with no benefit at this scale | Two separate services (e.g., Express API + React SPA) would require CORS config, separate deployments, and duplicated auth logic without runtime benefit for 50 users |
